explanation: I found no single Mathlib lemma that states this. `vlMoll n` is the library's own `CKN.mollifier` with ε = 1/(n+1), and that is defined as `(standardMollifier ε hε).normed volume`, Mathlib's normalized bump function (`ContDiffBump.normed`). The result says the integral of `|vlMoll n|` is 1. To get it from Mathlib you need two separate facts: `ContDiffBump.nonneg_normed`, to drop the absolute value, and `ContDiffBump.integral_normed`, for the integral being 1. You also have to unfold two library definitions. I listed every `normed` lemma in `Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/BumpFunction/Normed.lean`. None of them states the integral of the absolute value (or norm) of `f.normed` directly, so one declaration plus routine glue is not enough. Most of the content also sits in the library's own definitions.
